questions.decisive_words: per-customer order, several consumers, dedicated throughput, uneven growth
questions.reusable_rule: Align partition keys with the ordering scope, scale shard capacity, and isolate demanding consumers with enhanced fan-out.

questions.stem: An application writes compliance reports to S3. Reports are read daily for thirty days, about monthly through day ninety, and rarely afterward, but any later retrieval must begin in milliseconds. The company wants to minimize storage cost without rewriting the application. Which lifecycle design is most appropriate?

options.A: Keep reports in S3 Standard initially, transition them to S3 Standard-IA after thirty days, and then to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after ninety days.
options.B: Move reports to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after one day and promise millisecond retrieval.
options.C: Move reports to S3 One Zone-IA immediately even though the compliance copy cannot tolerate loss of one Availability Zone.
options.D: Keep every report in S3 Standard forever because lifecycle transitions cannot preserve the object key.

rationales.A: Correct. The transitions match declining known access while preserving millisecond access and multi-AZ durability, subject to class minimums.
rationales.B: Deep Archive retrieval normally takes hours and therefore violates the millisecond access requirement.
rationales.C: One Zone-IA stores data in one Availability Zone and is unsuitable when the only compliance copy needs multi-AZ resilience.
rationales.D: Lifecycle transitions preserve object access semantics and can reduce storage cost as access declines.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce S3 report storage cost over time while preserving millisecond retrieval and resilient storage.
questions.decisive_words: daily thirty days, monthly to ninety, rarely, milliseconds
questions.reusable_rule: Choose lifecycle classes from access frequency, retrieval-time, resilience, and minimum-duration requirements together.

questions.stem: A fleet uses general-purpose EBS volumes whose capacity was increased only to obtain more baseline IOPS. The workload now has known IOPS and throughput needs but does not require provisioned-IOPS durability. Which change can reduce cost while preserving performance?

options.A: Migrate to magnetic standard volumes and assume they provide the same latency and IOPS.
options.B: Use io2 Block Express for every volume regardless of required durability or IOPS.
options.C: Migrate to EBS gp3 and configure volume size, IOPS, and throughput independently.
options.D: Copy the block devices to S3 Glacier and attach the archive directly to EC2.

rationales.A: Previous-generation magnetic volumes do not provide equivalent general-purpose SSD performance.
rationales.B: io2 can provide higher durability and IOPS but may add unnecessary cost for the stated requirements.
rationales.C: Correct. gp3 separates performance settings from capacity, avoiding gp2 overprovisioning solely for IOPS.
rationales.D: S3 Glacier is object archive storage and cannot be attached as an EBS block device.

questions.central_requirement: Stop overprovisioning EBS capacity solely to obtain general-purpose SSD performance.
questions.decisive_words: capacity increased for IOPS, known IOPS and throughput, no io2 need
questions.reusable_rule: Use gp3 when general-purpose block workloads benefit from sizing capacity and performance independently.

questions.stem: A shared Amazon EFS file system contains project files that are active for two weeks and then are usually untouched for months. Occasional later access can tolerate a small first-byte latency increase. Which configuration reduces storage cost with minimal application change?

options.A: Provision maximum EFS throughput permanently because higher throughput lowers storage price.
options.B: Copy every file to EC2 instance store after two weeks and delete the EFS file system.
options.C: Convert the file system into an EBS root volume attached simultaneously to all instances in multiple Availability Zones.
options.D: Enable EFS lifecycle management to transition inactive files to an EFS infrequent-access or archive class.

rationales.A: Throughput mode affects performance billing and does not make active EFS storage cheaper in this manner.
rationales.B: Instance store is ephemeral and not a shared durable replacement for EFS.
rationales.C: An EBS root volume cannot be mounted as one shared cross-AZ file system by all instances.
rationales.D: Correct. EFS lifecycle management transparently moves inactive files to lower-cost storage classes.

questions.central_requirement: Lower the cost of inactive shared files while preserving the EFS interface.
questions.decisive_words: active two weeks, untouched for months, occasional access
questions.reusable_rule: Use EFS lifecycle policies when file access cools over time and applications should retain the same file-system interface.

questions.stem: A solutions architect is comparing Amazon S3 storage classes for cost optimization. Which statements are correct?

options.A: S3 Intelligent-Tiering always charges a retrieval fee for objects in its frequent access tier.
options.B: S3 Standard stores every object in only one Availability Zone to reduce cost.
options.C: S3 Standard-IA has no retrieval charge and no minimum storage duration considerations.
options.D: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval provides millisecond retrieval for rarely accessed archive data.
options.E: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone and is appropriate only when that resilience tradeoff is acceptable.
options.F: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term archives whose retrieval can take hours.

rationales.A: The frequent and infrequent automatic access tiers do not impose the claimed universal retrieval charge behavior.
rationales.B: S3 Standard is designed for multi-AZ resilience rather than single-zone placement.
rationales.C: Standard-IA includes retrieval and minimum-duration considerations that must be included in cost analysis.
rationales.D: Correct. Glacier Instant Retrieval combines archive pricing characteristics with millisecond access.
rationales.E: Correct. One Zone-IA costs less by using one Availability Zone, so data must be reproducible or tolerate that risk.
rationales.F: Correct. Deep Archive targets very infrequent long-term retention with retrieval measured in hours.

questions.central_requirement: Distinguish S3 storage-class cost, retrieval, and resilience characteristics.
questions.decisive_words: One Zone, retrieval time, archive, minimum duration
questions.reusable_rule: Select an S3 class only after matching access frequency, retrieval latency, resilience, and minimum-duration economics.

questions.stem: A fault-tolerant rendering farm runs independent jobs that checkpoint to S3 and can resume after interruption. Demand varies widely, and the company wants the lowest EC2 compute cost without committing to a fixed instance family. Which design is most appropriate?

options.A: Use only On-Demand Instances and disable scaling during low demand.
options.B: Use an EC2 Auto Scaling group with diversified Spot Instance capacity and interruption-aware workers.
options.C: Run the entire farm on Dedicated Hosts at fixed maximum capacity.
options.D: Purchase a zonal Reserved Instance for one exact type before measuring demand.

rationales.A: On-Demand capacity is flexible but does not provide the lowest cost for interruption-tolerant batch work.
rationales.B: Correct. Diversified Spot capacity fits interruption-tolerant, checkpointed jobs and reduces cost without a long-term type commitment.
rationales.C: Dedicated Hosts add cost and are intended for licensing or isolation needs not stated here.
rationales.D: A specific zonal reservation reduces flexibility and is premature for highly variable, diversified demand.

questions.central_requirement: Minimize EC2 cost for checkpointed independent jobs that tolerate interruption.
questions.decisive_words: fault-tolerant, checkpoint, resume, variable, no fixed family
questions.reusable_rule: Use diversified Spot capacity for interruption-tolerant work and design the worker to checkpoint and resume safely.

questions.stem: A service has a steady compute baseline, unpredictable customer-facing peaks that cannot be interrupted, and a separate retryable batch queue. The company can commit to one year but expects instance families and Regions to change. Which purchasing mix is most cost effective?

options.A: Purchase zonal Reserved Instances for peak capacity in one exact Availability Zone and run batch only on On-Demand.
options.B: Run all three demand categories on Dedicated Hosts without a licensing requirement.
options.C: Cover the steady eligible baseline with a Compute Savings Plan, use On-Demand capacity for noninterruptible excess, and use Spot for retryable batch workers.
options.D: Use Spot for the customer-facing baseline and discard requests whenever Spot capacity is reclaimed.

rationales.A: Committing to the full peak and one zone wastes capacity and reduces the flexibility explicitly required.
rationales.B: Dedicated Hosts introduce substantial cost without a stated compliance or licensing benefit.
rationales.C: Correct. Compute Savings Plans preserve compute flexibility, On-Demand handles uncertain critical peaks, and Spot discounts tolerant batch work.
rationales.D: Spot interruption can remove customer-facing baseline capacity and discarding requests is unacceptable.

questions.central_requirement: Optimize steady, critical burst, and retryable batch compute with different pricing models.
questions.decisive_words: steady baseline, peaks cannot interrupt, retryable batch, families and Regions change
questions.reusable_rule: Apply commitments to the stable baseline, On-Demand to uncertain critical demand, and Spot to interruption-tolerant capacity.

questions.stem: A lightweight report function runs for one minute every hour, has no local state, and needs 512 MB of memory. The company wants to avoid paying for idle servers and minimize operating effort. Which compute option is most cost effective?

options.A: Keep a large On-Demand EC2 instance running continuously.
options.B: Run the code as a scheduled AWS Lambda function.
options.C: Purchase a Dedicated Host for the report function.
options.D: Run an always-on Amazon ECS cluster with several unused EC2 container instances.

rationales.A: A continuously running EC2 instance incurs idle cost and operating work between hourly executions.
rationales.B: Correct. Lambda bills for requests and execution duration and removes idle server management for this short periodic task.
rationales.C: A Dedicated Host is far more capacity and cost than the tiny stateless workload requires.
rationales.D: Unused container hosts create the same idle-capacity problem the company wants to avoid.

questions.central_requirement: Avoid idle compute cost for a short, stateless, hourly task.
questions.decisive_words: one minute every hour, no state, avoid idle servers
questions.reusable_rule: For short intermittent stateless execution, compare serverless duration billing before provisioning always-on hosts.

questions.stem: A company runs a steady production RDS database and several development databases used only during business hours. Performance data shows the production instance is oversized, and the company can make a one-year commitment after rightsizing. Which actions can reduce database cost?

options.A: Purchase an appropriate Reserved DB Instance after the stable production requirement is right-sized.
options.B: Keep every development database running all night to preserve billing discounts.
options.C: Buy a Reserved DB Instance for the current oversized production shape before reviewing utilization.
options.D: Stop eligible development DB instances outside business hours and account for automatic restart behavior.
options.E: Create additional read replicas even though there is no read-performance requirement.
options.F: Right-size the production DB instance based on measured CPU, memory, and I/O demand.

rationales.A: Correct. A reservation can reduce cost for the stable, measured production baseline after rightsizing.
rationales.B: Idle development databases continue to incur compute cost and are not required for the stated production commitment.
rationales.C: Committing to an oversized shape locks in avoidable waste and reverses the correct optimization order.
rationales.D: Correct. Stopping eligible development instances reduces idle compute charges, with schedules designed around service restart limits.
rationales.E: Unneeded replicas add database instance and storage cost without solving a performance requirement.
rationales.F: Correct. Rightsizing removes persistent unused capacity before applying any commitment.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce cost for a steady production database and business-hours development databases.
questions.decisive_words: oversized production, one-year commitment, development business hours
questions.reusable_rule: Right-size first, commit only the stable baseline, and schedule nonproduction databases when service constraints allow.

questions.stem: A new DynamoDB workload has unpredictable request volume and no reliable capacity forecast. The team wants the table to scale automatically and prefers request-based billing until a stable pattern emerges. Which capacity mode should it choose?

options.A: DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode
options.B: A fixed EC2 instance that proxies every table request
options.C: DynamoDB provisioned mode with no auto scaling and zero write capacity
options.D: S3 Glacier Deep Archive retrieval capacity

rationales.A: Correct. On-demand mode automatically accommodates traffic and bills for read and write requests without capacity planning.
rationales.B: An EC2 proxy adds cost and does not replace DynamoDB capacity mode selection.
rationales.C: A fixed provisioned configuration without scaling can throttle unpredictable traffic and still requires forecasting.
rationales.D: Glacier retrieval capacity is unrelated to DynamoDB table request processing.

questions.central_requirement: Select DynamoDB billing and scaling for an unpredictable new workload.
questions.decisive_words: unpredictable, no forecast, automatically, request-based billing
questions.reusable_rule: Start with on-demand for unknown spiky DynamoDB demand and revisit provisioned economics when usage becomes predictable.

questions.stem: A production ElastiCache replication group has run at a stable size for a year and is expected to remain unchanged for three more years. The company wants a billing discount without changing cache behavior or reducing availability. What should it do?

options.A: Replace the replication group with Spot EC2 instances and accept cache loss during every interruption.
options.B: Move the hot cache data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
options.C: Increase node count first so a larger reservation produces a larger percentage discount.
options.D: Purchase reserved nodes that match the stable ElastiCache node configuration and term.

rationales.A: Self-managed Spot nodes alter operations and availability and do not preserve the managed replication-group behavior.
rationales.B: Deep Archive cannot provide in-memory cache latency.
rationales.C: Artificially increasing capacity raises total cost even if the discount percentage appears larger.
rationales.D: Correct. Reserved nodes provide a billing discount for predictable, sustained ElastiCache usage without changing runtime behavior.

questions.central_requirement: Discount a stable long-running ElastiCache footprint without changing its architecture.
questions.decisive_words: stable size, three years, billing discount, preserve availability
questions.reusable_rule: Use service reservations for a measured stable baseline, not as a reason to provision unnecessary capacity.

questions.stem: A media site stores popular objects in S3 and serves a global audience. Direct origin downloads create high data-transfer cost and latency. Some query parameters are tracking-only, while signed authorization data must still be validated. Which architecture best balances cost, performance, and access control?

options.A: Serve content through CloudFront, exclude tracking-only values from the cache key, preserve required authorization behavior, and protect the S3 origin with origin access control.
options.B: Replicate every object to EC2 instance store in all Regions and bypass caching.
options.C: Make S3 public and add every query parameter, cookie, and header to a unique cache key.
options.D: Place a NAT gateway in every viewer network and route browser downloads through the gateways.

rationales.A: Correct. CloudFront reduces repeated origin transfer, an intentional cache key improves reuse, and origin access control keeps S3 private.
rationales.B: Manual instance-store replicas are ephemeral, operationally expensive, and lack managed global caching.
rationales.C: Public S3 weakens access control, and an overbroad cache key reduces hits and cost efficiency.
rationales.D: NAT gateways are VPC egress resources and cannot be deployed in viewer networks as a CDN.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce global S3 delivery cost and latency without weakening private-origin authorization.
questions.decisive_words: global audience, origin transfer cost, tracking parameters, signed authorization
questions.reusable_rule: Use CloudFront for cacheable global delivery, minimize the cache key safely, and keep the origin private with explicit origin authorization.

questions.stem: Private application subnets in three Availability Zones send heavy traffic to S3, DynamoDB, and Secrets Manager, plus a small amount of general internet traffic. The company wants lower NAT processing cost without creating a single zonal egress dependency. Which changes should be made?

options.A: Remove every egress path, including the path required for the remaining internet destinations.
options.B: Create S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints and associate them with the relevant private route tables.
options.C: Create interface VPC endpoints for Secrets Manager in the required Availability Zones with private DNS.
options.D: Route S3 and DynamoDB traffic through one NAT gateway in a fourth subnet.
options.E: Keep a resilient same-AZ NAT path for only the general internet traffic that cannot use an endpoint.
options.F: Send Secrets Manager API calls through a public Application Load Balancer.

rationales.A: The application still requires limited general internet egress, so removing every path breaks a stated requirement.
rationales.B: Correct. Gateway endpoints remove supported S3 and DynamoDB traffic from NAT processing without hourly endpoint charges.
rationales.C: Correct. A Secrets Manager interface endpoint keeps API calls private and avoids NAT for that service.
rationales.D: Centralizing heavy service traffic through one NAT increases processing and cross-AZ exposure rather than reducing it.
rationales.E: Correct. Per-AZ or otherwise resilient same-AZ NAT routing preserves zonal egress for traffic that truly needs internet translation.
rationales.F: An Application Load Balancer cannot proxy arbitrary Secrets Manager control-plane calls and would expose unnecessary public infrastructure.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce NAT charges for AWS service traffic while retaining resilient egress for remaining internet destinations.
questions.decisive_words: heavy S3 DynamoDB Secrets Manager, small internet traffic, no single zonal dependency
questions.reusable_rule: Use VPC endpoints for supported AWS services and reserve zonally resilient NAT capacity for destinations that actually require internet egress.

questions.stem: EC2 instances run in private subnets across three Availability Zones. Every subnet routes outbound traffic through one NAT gateway in the first Availability Zone, creating high cross-AZ data processing charges and a zonal dependency. What change best addresses both concerns?

options.A: Keep one NAT gateway and move every application instance into its Availability Zone.
options.B: Deploy a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each private subnet to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.
options.C: Send outbound connections through an S3 bucket configured as a website endpoint.
options.D: Replace the NAT gateway with an internet gateway attached directly to private instances without public addresses.

rationales.A: Concentrating all compute in one zone sacrifices application resilience and does not meet the multi-AZ design intent.
rationales.B: Correct. Same-AZ NAT routing avoids unnecessary cross-AZ traversal and removes dependence on one zonal NAT gateway.
rationales.C: An S3 website endpoint cannot perform general outbound network address translation.
rationales.D: An internet gateway does not provide source translation for private instances without public addresses.

questions.central_requirement: Reduce cross-AZ NAT cost and remove a single-zonal egress dependency.
questions.decisive_words: three Availability Zones, one NAT, cross-AZ charges, zonal dependency
questions.reusable_rule: For resilient NAT gateway egress, deploy per Availability Zone and route private subnets to their local zonal gateway.
